description: Restriction of the use of polythene and plastic in the Sri Pada highly sensitive ecological zone
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-12-22 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- The Sri Pada pilgrimage season begins in December every year and lasts for 6 months, during which, a large amount of biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste, disposed of by pilgrims and other people, accumulates in the area. The Sri Pada site is a high-sensitive area covered by the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance, and waste management in the area is a timely requirement. Accordingly, upon the Minister of Environment informing the Cabinet that the Ministry of Environment would adopt the following measures from 2025 to minimize the use of polythene and plastic in the said area during the Sri Pada pilgrimage season, it was decided to grant the concurrence of the Cabinet for the same:

Lunch sheets, containers made of high-density polyethylene (squeeze bags), sachet packets, single-use food containers made of expanded polystyrene, single-use drinking straws, straws, single-use plates, cups, spoons, forks and knives, which are made of already banned polythene, will be completely prohibited from being sold in this area or carried by pilgrims.
Prohibition of carrying single-use plastic water bottles and beverage bottles of less than 1 litre.
Prohibiting the disposal of food, beverage, medicine or other goods with polythene covers and packaging in the environmentally sensitive zone.
Assigning the responsibility of managing the waste generated after the sale of food, beverages, medicine or other merchandise with plastic covers sold by business establishments in the environmentally highly sensitive zone to the relevant shop owners.
Prohibiting the contamination of water sources and waterways and the disposal of polythene and plastic waste in those places.
Assigning the responsibility of properly collecting the polythene and plastic waste accumulated during the construction and maintenance of shops and bringing it outside the Sri Pada highly sensitive zone, to the respective shop owners for final disposal through the relevant Urban Councils or Pradeshiya Sabhas.
